claims.text: Adding molybdenum to CoCrFeNi will promote nucleation of a MoS2-rich tribofilm during sliding.
The MoS2-rich tribofilm will remain stable from room temperature to 800 °C.
Spark plasma sintering can be used to introduce the proposed molybdenum addition and produce a CoCrFeNiMo material.
Molybdenum addition may also lead to Cr2O3 phases associated with the tribofilm.
Friction-induced heating will drive an in-situ reaction between added Mo and sulfur sources.
Pre-incorporated MoS2 could supply sulfur for tribofilm formation.
Trace atmospheric sulfur in ambient air could supply enough sulfur to form the proposed MoS2-rich tribofilm.
The in-situ Mo-sulfur reaction will produce a continuous lubricating layer.
The tribofilm will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reducing direct metal-to-metal contact through the tribofilm will retard wear.
Molybdenum addition will refine the CoCrFeNi microstructure.
Molybdenum addition will improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of CoCrFeNi.
CoCrFeNiMo will have a lower coefficient of friction than baseline CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
CoCrFeNiMo will have a lower wear rate than baseline CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The predicted benefit is bounded to ambient-air sliding under moderate load and speed, exemplified by a normal force of about 10 N.
Changing load, atmosphere, or other extreme test conditions may change the predicted performance.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as an optimized molybdenum addition, but the uncertainty field states that the optimal molybdenum concentration remains unknown.

The stated single intervention is elemental molybdenum addition, whereas the mechanism invokes pre-incorporated MoS2 as a possible sulfur source; pre-incorporating MoS2 would constitute an additional, unstated intervention.
